body: In the vendor repo it seems like we typically put cleanup code in extension wrapper deconstructors, so in the space warp extension wrapper it calls `unregister_projection_views_extension(this)` if the extension is enabled, etc. I really don't know how necessary that is (probably not since it's also in `instance_destroyed`?) but just something I noticed.
I feel like having this comment above every (or any!) `frame_synthesis_ext` check is overkill. There's a fair number of them and I, personally, would remove them.
Add an early return here if `enabled == p_enabled`?
Add an early return here if `relax_frame_interval == p_relax_frame_interval`?
Checking `!render_state.skip_next_frame` here with the early return above is redundant.

body:
Owh misread, I thought I didn't do the cleanup at all, but I'm doing it in `on_session_destroyed`.

I tent to mirror things, so if I register something in `on_session_created`, I do the opposite in `on_session_destroyed`.

I guess we can move it earlier. I'm not a fan of doing it in the constructor/destructor because Godot will instance an object in the editor so it can get the class info for the online help system. This tends to lead to issues because OpenXR is not setup.

But maybe move it into instance create/destroy?
I agree, this is out of habit and it made loads of sense when we had our first extensions. But by now, its real overkill :)

```suggestion
void OpenXRFrameSynthesisExtension::_set_render_state_enabled_rt(bool p_enabled) {
```

void OpenXRFrameSynthesisExtension::_set_relax_frame_interval_rt(bool p_relax_frame_interval) {

The other option would be to add the viewcount as a parameter to `set_view_configuration_and_get_next_pointer` but that may be too breaking...
